## ACCEPT — PM review (step 7)

### File surface
14 files, which reconciles with the report's "6 changed source files" (that figure is its ESLint scope — 3 source + 3 test):

| group | files |
|---|---|
| **source (3)** | `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (+64) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (+74/−26) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (+43/−7) |
| **tests (3)** | `packages/objectql/src/save-meta-response-conformance.test.ts` (+206) · `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts` (+102) · `packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` (+17/−3) |
| **generated (7)** | `packages/spec/{api-surface,authorable-surface,export-origins,json-schema.manifest}/api.json` · `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` · `content/docs/references/index.mdx` · `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts.md` |
| **changeset (1)** | `.changeset/runtime-gate-advisories-on-save-response.md` |

All seven generated entries are `os-regen`-family artifacts and are consistent with the source change — `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness` and `Build Docs` are all green, so they were regenerated rather than hand-edited. No `content/docs/releases/`, no `docs/adr/**`.

### CI, per job
26 check runs, all `completed`: **25 `success`**, **1 `skipped`** (`Console Pin Gate`, path-filtered). Both required gates read on their own conclusions: **`ESLint` success (11:09:35Z)**, **`TypeScript Type Check` success (11:21:24Z)**. Also green: `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core` 3/3 + rollup, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 3/3 + rollup, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `ADR maintainer approval`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`.

### The four ruled constraints, each verifiable in the diff
`advisories` optional on `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema` reusing the D3 element shape ✓ · emitted **only when non-empty**, never `[]` ✓ · `rulesRun` off ✓ · save door only, with the publish-door asymmetry stated in the changeset ✓. The channel exists where I priced it: `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns a `RuntimeAuthoringVerdict` record instead of `Error | null`, so the success path finally has somewhere to put a value.

**One thing better than I asked for**: rather than adding the field alongside the existing hand-written `RuntimeAuthoringIssue` interface, `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` is declared once in `packages/spec` and `metadata-protocol` **re-exports** it. That removes a parallel definition instead of creating a second one — the contract-first direction, done without being told.

### The cross-seat `packages/spec` declaration
Carried under the #5586 declare-and-proceed precedent, in its own top section of the PR body, naming **#6017** with the veto open until merge. That is the shape I committed to on the card and on #6017, and it is prominent rather than buried. If that seat wants it back at any point before merge, this PR yields.

### Reverse verification — the strongest of this term

**Predicted red, came out red**, five probes with real messages: R1 (spec field removed) `expected [ 'advisories' ] to deeply equal []`; R2 (producer spread disabled) `Target cannot be null or undefined.`; R5 (producer-only key rename) 1 red; R6' (drop `hint` from the shared element) shape mismatch. R5's caveat is reported honestly — direction right, but the first failing assertion was `toHaveLength(1)`, not the `strippedKeys` message predicted.

⭐ **R4 turns the ruling's caveat from an argument into a measurement.** The maintainer's ruling accepted, as a stated cost, that the field must be conditional and therefore the existing conformance gate would *not* go red to remind anyone the declaration was missing. R4 emitted `advisories: []` unconditionally — the ruled-forbidden refactor — and measured **3 failed / 7 passed: the three new absence pins red, and all five pre-existing #5745 cases GREEN**. That is direct evidence that the existing gate is structurally blind to this class, which is exactly why the declaration had to be deliberate. The caveat is no longer something we assert; it is something we measured.

⭐ **The previously-unmeasured variant is now measured.** I carried forward, twice, that "does a conditionally-added key leave the three existing conformance cases green" had been flagged unmeasured rather than assumed. It is now measured in both directions — green with the declaration and without it (R1) — and the case is named in the file `GUARD (green either way): a clean view save is untouched by the new field`, with a docblock stating the existing gate cannot go red on a missing declaration. Labelled as a guard, not counted as evidence.

⭐ **A probe was caught invalidating itself, and reported.** R1's first run redirected the spec build to `/dev/null`; the build had **failed**, the test read stale `dist`, and it reported a false `10 passed`. That is this lane's operational note 24 (never swallow stderr on a command whose output is evidence) and the stale-artefact trap of #7000, landing on the dev — and the dev caught it, said so, and re-ran visibly. The re-run then exposed a **third diagnostic nobody predicted**: `build-schemas.ts`'s authorable-surface ratchet refuses the removal at **build time** (`❌ 1 authorable key(s) disappeared from the contract`), before any test executes. A run that had accepted the first green would have shipped with a false confidence reading and never learned the build-time gate exists.

⭐ **A missed prediction produced a real coverage finding rather than an excuse.** R6' narrowed the shared element and metadata-protocol did **not** go red. The measured cause: that package has no typecheck script and `tsup` never type-checks (#4311), so no `tsc` program exists over that file — meaning **the type-level binding of the re-export is not checked anywhere today**. Reported plainly instead of dressed up. I am recording this rather than filing a new card, because it is an instance of the known #4311 gap, not a new one; the runtime binding is real and pinned, the type-level one rests on #4311 being closed.

**Unmeasured, stated and not counted as passed**: R6 (restoring `=> Error | null`) not run, no information beyond R2; the REST wire not driven against a live server, so the "200" claim is protocol-level; the publish door deliberately not probed (it rides behind #7294 by ruling).

### Ruling
ACCEPT. Flip to ready + auto-merge (SQUASH) is queued behind a GraphQL rate limit along with #7429's — reads are on a separate quota, which is why this review posted. ⚠️ Two landing notes for whoever executes the queue: this PR touches `os-regen`-family generated artifacts, so if it is rebuilt against a moved `main` the regeneration must be redone wholesale rather than text-merged; and `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` carries a count assertion that any concurrent spec PR will conflict with — an ejection there is the expected shape, re-resolved by recounting from the merged file rather than by arithmetic on either side's receipt.
